title: SCANOSS Crypto-Finder Callgraph Export (interned frames)
description: Interned callgraph export, the local CLI default of --export-callgraph. Chain frames omit catalog identity; join through functions[] plus finding_graphs[].call_chain_indexes. scan_metadata.ecosystems lists every call graph analyzed when first-party findings span more than one supported ecosystem. 6.17 adds finding_graphs[].dependency, the analysis route counts and evidence, root_kind on a chain's first frame, and three unresolved_reason values. 6.18 adds a chain frame's excerpt, excerpt_unavailable, entry_call.call_site_column and, on a chain's first frame, entry_rule.

schema_version.description: Interned callgraph contract, the local CLI default. The inlined compatibility render remains 6.14.

finding_graphs.description: One reachability record per interim-report finding.

supporting_calls.description: Lifecycle and context calls associated with findings.

functions.description: Interned callable identity catalog. finding_graphs[].call_chain_indexes are 0-based positions into this array. Schema 6.15 keeps catalog identity here instead of on call_chains frames.

crypto_entry_points.description: Reverse-reachability index keyed by callable identity: every function from which a finding is reachable, deliberately broader than the exported call_chains. crypto_entry_points[].root marks the chain roots.

root.description: True when this entry point is where a chain starts: the first root-module caller in dependency mode, or an in-degree-zero graph root in standalone mode.

unresolved_reason.description: Why the finding could not be attributed (no_containing_function, no_crypto_call_match, language_not_analyzed, with finding_location), or why an attributed finding's reachability is unknown: a depth limit cut every route (traversal_truncated), every route crosses a name_only edge (unresolved_dispatch), or every route from the application to the finding's dependency crosses a dependency without source (dependency_without_source). Stitched exports carry unresolved_dispatch only.

call_chain_indexes.description: Index-based routes matching call_chains order. Each inner array lists functions[] indexes for that walk.

root_kind.description: On a chain's first frame only, what that frame is: a program entry point (main), a method a framework calls (framework_entry), an application function no application code calls (no_callers; a graph root on a library scanned alone), or the frame where a depth limit stopped the walk (depth_limit). The stitched export writes it too when the fragments recorded entry kinds (graph-fragment-1.14), never depth_limit.

entry_rule.description: On a main or framework_entry first frame only, the ID of the entry-point catalog entry that recognized it: <language>/<framework>:<shape>[:<directory>]:<first name>, as java/spring:decorator:RequestMapping. Absent when language semantics made the frame an entry point (a main function, an override of an external type), and on the stitched export.

excerpt_unavailable.description: Why the frame has no excerpt: its file is not in the scanned tree or a dependency source directory the scan resolved, or the export has no source (no_source; the stitched export writes it on every frame), reading the file failed (unreadable), or the focus line is not a line of the file (out_of_range). Absent when excerpt is present.

entry_call.description: The call in the previous frame that leads to this one. Absent on a chain's first frame.

call_site_column.description: 1-based column the call expression starts at on line. Written by the live export when the parser recorded it.

ecosystems.description: Every call graph the export analyzed, the primary ecosystem first. Present only when first-party findings span more than one supported ecosystem; ecosystem, root_module, function_count and edge_count above stay those of the primary graph.

FindingDependency.description: The dependency a dependency finding sits in and how the application reaches it in the resolved dependency graph, not in the call graph. Absent on first-party findings.

purl.description: Package URL of the dependency, versioned when the version is known.

relationship.description: Absent when the dependency graph was not resolved or does not connect the dependency to the application.

path.description: Shortest route from the application to this dependency: a direct dependency first, this dependency last, the application (scan_metadata.root_module) not listed. A route through dependencies parsed with source is preferred. Absent with relationship.

without_source.description: The dependency joined the call graph without source code (types only for Java, not at all elsewhere), so no call chain crosses it. Live export only.

FindingAnalysis.description: Completeness of the finding's call_chains and parameters, and how many routes support the verdict and how strongly they were resolved.

paths_total.description: Distinct routes from a chain root to the finding the call graph holds; chains that differ only in a call-site line count once. Saturates at the largest int64 and is then a lower bound. Live export only, with a route.

paths_kept.description: How many of those routes call_chains shows. Live export only, with a route.

route_evidence.description: Strength of the finding's strongest route, rated by its weakest call: every call resolved statically (direct), at least one interface or subclass dispatch and no name_only call (dispatch), or every route needs a name_only call (name_only, with unresolved_reason unresolved_dispatch).

no_callers_only.description: Every root of the routes supporting the verdict has root_kind no_callers. Omitted when false. The stitched export sets it only when the fragments recorded entry kinds (graph-fragment-1.14).

Excerpt.description: Up to seven lines of the source the analysis read, centered on the frame's focus line: the call that leads to the next frame, the crypto call on the last frame, or the function's first line when neither is known. Clipped to the file's bounds.

focus_line.description: The line the frame's evidence points at, within the window.

lines.description: Verbatim lines without line endings, each cut to 240 characters.

truncated.description: True when at least one line was cut at 240 characters.
